### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-dev`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-i18n.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/environment-routing.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackDefinitionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/automation/hook-bodies.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackDefinitionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/concepts/north-star.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackDefinitionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackDefinitionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/examples.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackDefinitionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via resolveArtifactPackageOrder (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackDefinitionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackDefinitionSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-dev/src/dev-i18n.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **148** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json beac7980267a361c5979ca7aa75c034624955af0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9c07e54389b375ea44031f82d2439f286cfc8948` — the merge of head `d780d37e7cccb95f1b21fa93220d0b9b19d375d8` into base `beac7980267a361c5979ca7aa75c034624955af0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9c07e54389b375ea44031f82d2439f286cfc8948 && git checkout 9c07e54389b375ea44031f82d2439f286cfc8948
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin beac7980267a361c5979ca7aa75c034624955af0 d780d37e7cccb95f1b21fa93220d0b9b19d375d8 && git checkout -B drift-repro beac7980267a361c5979ca7aa75c034624955af0 && git merge --no-ff d780d37e7cccb95f1b21fa93220d0b9b19d375d8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json beac7980267a361c5979ca7aa75c034624955af0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs beac7980267a361c5979ca7aa75c034624955af0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ccd0c405ccd59e641ecf816b0ec1caa7ba6f43b2`

<sub>Reviewed and posted 2026-09-23T20:54Z by the at-tier review subagent the `domain:spec#5` seat spawned. Inputs: card #15293 with its 12 comments (rulings `5634034754`, `5644710907` on #15292, correction `5763171190`, unblock `5798034561`, dev report `5801982470`, seat answers `5802045574`), #19925, #19926, the PR (diff, body, 3 commits, 46 check-runs, 1 comment), `AGENTS.md`, `contract-review.md`. Method: detached worktrees at the head and at the merge-base `8490127962` (the PR base GitHub reports is main's tip, not the fork point); a 22-input × 7-reader differential and a caller-level probe run under the runtime package's src-aliased vitest on BOTH trees; every ablation re-applied by me and restored (both trees clean afterwards); `composeStacks` and `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` measured on the built spec dist. (read / ran / NOT MEASURED is marked per cell.)</sub>

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set — ran, before/after.** 6 of 154 cells moved between merge-base and head, all of them runtime `resolveArtifactCollections` on `{}` / `0` / `'x'` (with and without top-level collections): identity before → `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES` / 422 after. Every other cell is byte-equal on both trees: absent, explicit `undefined`, `null` → identity (runtime), `[artifact]` (core), `false` / `undefined` (plugin-dev), `undefined` or the top-level default (plugin-security); `[]` → identity / `[]`; well-formed `packages[]` → the same merged `objects` on both trees; malformed entry → `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGE_ENTRY` everywhere on both trees; `null`, `undefined`, a string, a number as the artifact → identity on both. Right under ruling A: yes. Nothing that loaded before stops loading except the three ruled values, and `packages: null` is untouched as #19926 requires. Emitter census (mine, `git grep` over tracked ts/js/json for a non-array `packages:` literal): 0 artifact-shaped hits (an esbuild option, route tables, the spec merge-strategy table, script fixtures); the 2 JSON files carrying a `packages` key are docs nav and shard timings. The schema refuses `{}`, `0`, `'x'` and `null` (`invalid_type`) and accepts absent, `[]` and well-formed — ran on the built dist; the declaration line is untouched by the diff.

**Sites that read `packages` on an artifact or stack — my enumeration, `grep` over `packages/` and `apps/` excluding tests.** Refuse through the resolver (the single raise site of `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES`, measured 1): core `artifact-packages.ts`; runtime `artifact-collections.ts` (now); plugin-dev `dev-i18n.ts` (only when the package pass is reached — a stack whose top-level `translations` answers first returns `true` without reading `packages`, ran); plugin-security `app-default-permission-set.ts` (resolves first, so it refuses even when the top level names a default, ran); objectql `plugin.ts:427` and metadata `plugin.ts:975` (read: the `carriesPackages` stamp at `:974` is `Array.isArray` but the resolver call beside it refuses); runtime `security/artifact-granted-permissions.ts:131` (read); verify `declaredCollection` (ran: refuses when the top-level key is empty, answers the top level without reading `packages` when it is present — the same posture as plugin-dev). Refuse before any reader: `composeStacks`' concat pass for two or more inputs (`STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID`, ran for `{}`, `0`, `'x'`, `null`, default and preserve); ⚠️ for ONE input `composeStacks` returns the input by identity (`stack.zod.ts:4864`), so it is not a door there. **Still fall through, outside the PR's surface:** cli `stack-collections.ts:99` `packageBodies` (ran: `resolveStackCollection({…, packages: {}}, 'objects')` → `[]` on both trees), cli `collect-docs.ts:386/1054/1253` (read: `[]` / same reference), carried by #19925; lint `object-graph.ts:215` `recordsOf(stack.packages)` at 4 lint sites (read: `{}` → `[]`, and a non-empty map is read as a record list — a fourth reading) — carried by no card.

**Callers of `resolveArtifactCollections` — my enumeration (5 modules, 7 call sites; it is module-scope only, not on `@objectstack/runtime`'s export map).** (1) `AppPlugin.collections` getter, first read in `start()` after the objectql lookup, never in `init()` (read: `init()` ends at the `manifest` service's `register()`, which reaches the resolver). Ran with a stub context: `start()` succeeds before and throws `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES` after on `{}`/`0`/`'x'`; a malformed entry throws on both trees (lit). Under a kernel boot `initPluginWithTimeout` is try/finally with no catch, so the `init()` refusal aborts Phase 1 and `start()` never runs — no visible change. Under `DevPlugin`: ran `DevPlugin.init` on `{}`/`0`/`'x'` — boots, one `error` line from the i18n auto-detect, no throw (absent control: no error line); the child-`init()` and child-`start()` `error` lines (`Failed to init/start child plugin …`) are read, not run (the harness disables objectql). Acceptable: loud, correctly attributed. (2) `collectBundleHooks/Actions/FunctionEntries` (exported): propagate — acceptable. (3) `mergeRuntimeModule` / `loadArtifactBundle`: ran — merges before, `warn` + skip after on the three values; well-formed merges on both; a malformed entry warns on both (lit). ⚠️ The line reads `runtime module load FAILED` for an artifact-shape refusal (pre-existing label; the real message is carried) — mislabel, not this PR's, see ③. (4) `resolveProjectDatabaseUrl`: ran with an artifact declaring a default sqlite datasource at the top level — `config-datasource` before, `unified-default` after on the three values; absent/`null`/`[]`/well-formed stay `config-datasource` on both; a malformed entry is `unified-default` on both (lit). The decline is silent by design; the only consumers passing `artifactPath` are `os dev` and `os start`, both followed by the child boot that refuses at `createStandaloneStack:794` (read). `os migrate`'s pre-boot probe passes no `artifactPath` (read: `migrate-occupancy-gate.ts:26`), so it is not a surface. Only pre-boot side effect: `os dev` `mkdir -p`s the resolved URL's parent, now the unified default's (read, negligible). (5) `createStandaloneStack:794`, unguarded: refuses while building — NOT MEASURED end-to-end (needs a driver boot); read only.

**The two plugin readers — ran.** plugin-security guard dropped: old guard re-added → 0 of 22 cells differ from head and the pin file stays 27/27; `Array.isArray` guard re-added → 6 cells fall through and 4 pins red (the three rows plus "refused just the same when the top level named a default"). Behaviour-equal: confirmed. plugin-dev guard kept: deleted → exactly 1 pin red ("reads its `translations` ONCE"), the three refusal rows stay green (the resolver refuses without it); widened to `Array.isArray` → the 3 new pins red. ⚠️ Narrowed to `undefined`-only (my ablation): 18/18 green — nothing pins the guard's `null` half to the resolver's; "this line changes with it" is prose-bound. See ③.

**Pins — ran at head.** runtime 19/19, plugin-dev 18/18, plugin-security 27/27 (after building spec, core and objectql's closure in the worktree). Each row asserts `code` and `status: 422`; each file carries a lit control (well-formed resolves; absent / explicit `undefined` / `null` take the single-package branch). Runtime line reverted to `!Array.isArray` → 3 red / 16 green, controls green.

**Contract prose.** Beside `AssembledPackageBodySchema`: the two readings, the refusal code, and the `null` caveat are true (ran). The corrected `preservePackageEntries` note is true: the concat pass refuses first for every input count on which the function can run, and for one input neither runs (ran). ⛔ Two universal sentences there ("Every reader of a release artifact's `packages` points here and does not restate it", "every reader reaches it through that one function") and the changeset's exclusive sentence ("The runtime's collection reader was the one that answered differently") name no set and are false as a census: the cli and lint readers above neither point at the rule nor reach the resolver (cli ran: `[]`). The core docblock's "the one place every reader reaches that refusal through" is true as a raise-site count (1). Every other added or changed docblock sentence, the `packages.mdx` sentence (read: same `init()` branch, same code, `error` line names the app plugin), the commit messages and the PR body's measured claims (schema declaration at `stack.zod.ts:1623`; behaviour-equal drop; one red pin; three red runtime pins) check out against my own runs.

**Model identifiers.** Swept the diff, the three commit messages, the changeset, the PR title and body and the PR's one comment for 15 spellings: 0 hits. The commit trailer pair is the model-free form.

**CI — head check-runs, 46 runs, de-duplicated by name keeping the latest `started_at`: 35 names, 31 success, 4 skipped, 0 failed.** Skips: `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` — label-gated, `needs:pack-smoke` not on the PR; `Console Pin Gate` — `filter.console` false, no console-filter path in the diff; `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size` — the latest runs are `edited`-event runs whose job `if` excludes `edited` (the earlier `synchronize` runs of both succeeded). Derived gate family not re-run locally.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/runtime: patch` — right: a released package's reader pulled back to the declared schema is a bug fix. Core, plugin-dev, spec: docblocks and tests only, no behaviour moved (ran / read). plugin-security: guard dropped, 0 of 22 cells and 27/27 pins equal — no behaviour moved, no changeset owed. `Clause-②: no` with no arm is the correct spelling: Clause-② asks whether the card widens an accept set or enlarges a public surface, and pulling a consumer back to the declared contract does not trigger it (`execution-duties.md:65,99`); the contract (`packages: z.array(ArtifactPackageSchema).optional()`) is unchanged, and `resolveArtifactCollections` is not a published export. The `(narrowing)` arm is for a contract narrowing, which this is not.

### ③ Boundary flags

Blocking:
- **B1 — shipped census claims contradicted by measurement.** The changeset (ships in CHANGELOG): "The runtime's collection reader was the one that answered differently" — at head, cli `resolveStackCollection({ manifest, packages: {} }, 'objects')` returns `[]` (ran), `docsPackageRefs` / `bodyDocsOf` / `attachPackageDocs` return `[]` / the same reference (read), and lint `recordsOf` reads `{}` as `[]` and a map as records (read). The spec docblock (ships in the published `.d.ts`): "Every reader … points here and does not restate it" and "every reader reaches it through that one function" — same contradiction. The PR body says the opposite of the changeset ("Not in this PR: the cli readers"). Fix, one clause each: scope the changeset to the four readers ruling A names and say the cli readers are outstanding; make the two spec sentences normative ("must point here", "must reach it through") or name the outstanding set. Also give lint's `recordsOf` a carrier (#19925 widened, or a sibling).

Non-blocking:
- Q2 (guard kept): the kept guard is bound to the resolver's absent branch by prose only — narrowing it to `undefined`-only leaves 18/18 green (ran). Seat's A stands; #19926 carries `null`. Cheap hardening for the patch round: a plugin-dev pin asserting `stackDeclaresTranslations` and `resolveArtifactPackageOrder` give the same verdict on `{ packages: null }`.
- Q3 (dev-i18n refuses only what it reads): seat's A stands; measured (`withTop/{}` → `true`, the load path refuses). verify's `declaredCollection` has the same posture (ran) — consistent.
- Q1 (five "without / no `packages[]`" comments): seat's A stands; each scopes to the absent key.
- `mergeRuntimeModule` reports an artifact-shape refusal as "runtime module load FAILED" (pre-existing; `{}` now joins it; message text carried verbatim) — no carrier; a card is owed if the seat wants zero mislabels.
- Two stale sentences in the same `dev-i18n.ts` docblock the PR rewrites ("`new AppPlugin(this.options.stack)` parses the same object"; "the registration path IS reached from `AppPlugin.start`") are false per #15292's measurement and untouched here — fold into the patch round (two-line comment fix, same file).
- `composeStacks` with one input is identity (`:4864`): the dev report's "always emits an array" over-claims there (report only; the shipped note is true), and #19926's "`composeStacks` refused" row holds for two or more inputs.
- #19925 and #19926: carried, and both measured first-hand above (cli `[]`; schema refuses `null`, every reader reads it as absent).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-15293-non-array-packages-refusal`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Sfe5YjBLwB9J3y8fvm2xq1` — at-tier review subagent spawned by the `domain:spec#5` seat

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Head-sha: `d780d37e7cccb95f1b21fa93220d0b9b19d375d8`

<sub>Reviewed and posted 2026-09-23T22:03Z by the at-tier review subagent the `domain:spec#5` seat spawned. Inputs: card #15293 with its 13 comments (ruling `5634034754`, correction `5763171190`, unblock `5798034561`, dev reports `5801982470` / `5803274097`, seat answers `5802045574`), #15292's ruling `5644710907`, #19925 (+ `5802810217`), #19926 (+ `5802816661`), the PR (diff, body, 4 commits, 39 check-runs, 2 comments, prior record `5802780773`), `AGENTS.md`, `contract-review.md`. ### ① Derived judgments

**Sites that read `packages` on an artifact or stack — my grep over `packages/`, `apps/`, `scripts/`, tests excluded (0 hits under `apps/`).** Through the resolver (1 raise site, core `:214`, plus the ledger row): core; runtime (now); plugin-dev (only once the package pass is reached — a stack whose top-level `translations` answers first never reads `packages`, ran: `withTop/{}` → `true`); plugin-security (resolves first, refuses even when the top level names a default, ran); objectql `plugin.ts:427`, metadata `plugin.ts:975` (the `Array.isArray` stamp at `:974` sits beside an unguarded resolver call), runtime `security/artifact-granted-permissions.ts:131` (read); verify (ran: answers the top level when present, resolver otherwise). Still fall through: cli `stack-collections.ts:99`, `collect-docs.ts:385/1053/1252` (ran: `[]` on both trees) and lint `recordsOf` at 4 sites (ran: `{}` → `[]`, a map → records) — carried by #19925 with `5802810217`. Not artifact readers: cli `artifact-packages.ts:118` (a schema-parsed stack), `lower-callables.ts:315` (leaves the value for the parse after it), `cloud-connection:622` (an API response), rest route tables, `dev-plugin.ts:314`.

**Callers of `resolveArtifactCollections` — 5 modules, 7 call sites; module-private (not on `runtime/src/index.ts`). Ran, 8 inputs × 4 callers, 12 cells moved = `{}` / `0` / `'x'` × 4; absent, `null`, `[]`, well-formed unchanged; inlined entry equal on both trees (lit).** (1) `AppPlugin.collections`, first read in `start()` at `:668`, never in `init()`; `init()` ends at `manifest.register(servicePayload)` (`:394`), which reaches the resolver (objectql `:427`, read). `start()` with a stub context carrying `objectql`: OK before, `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES` after. (2) `collectBundleHooks/Actions/FunctionEntries/Functions` (exported): in-repo callers are `AppPlugin.start` after `collections` already threw, plus one cli test fixture — propagate, acceptable. (3) `mergeRuntimeModule` / `loadArtifactBundle`: merges before (`handler` a function); after, one `warn` line and the merge skipped (`handler` stays the string ref), as an inlined entry does on both trees. ⚠️ The line is labelled `runtime module load FAILED`, a pre-existing label the real message rides on — see ③. (4) `resolveProjectDatabaseUrl`: `config-datasource`/`db` before → `unified-default` after; absent / `null` / `[]` / well-formed stay `config-datasource`; inlined entry `unified-default` on both. Silent by design; callers passing `artifactPath` are `os dev`, `os start` and `createStandaloneStack:511` (read; `db clean` passes none), and each is followed by the artifact load that refuses. (5) `createStandaloneStack:794`, unguarded — ran over the same artifact file: builds before (`plugins` incl. `plugin.app.com.example.core`, leaving the refusal to `AppPlugin.init`), refuses `INVALID_ARTIFACT_PACKAGES` / 422 after; absent and well-formed build on both. `os dev` / `os start` / `os migrate` end to end through the cli: read, NOT MEASURED (needs the serve child; the runtime function they call is measured above).

**The two plugin readers — ran.** plugin-security: guard dropped — 0 of its 20 probe cells moved; pin file 27/27 at head and 27/27 with the old guard restored byte-exact; an `Array.isArray` guard → 4 red (the three rows + "refused just the same when the flattened top level already named a default"). Behaviour-equal: confirmed. plugin-dev: guard deleted → exactly 1 red (`reads its \`translations\` ONCE`); widened to `Array.isArray` → the 3 new rows red; ⚠️ narrowed to `undefined`-only → 18/18 green: the guard's `null` half is bound to the resolver's absent branch by prose only (③, carried by #19926's lockstep clause).

**Pins — ran at head.** runtime 19/19, plugin-dev 18/18, plugin-security 27/27; every row asserts `code` and `status: 422`; each file's lit control resolves a well-formed `packages[]` and takes the single-package branch for absent / explicit `undefined` / `null`. Runtime line reverted → 3 red / 16 green, controls green.

**Contract prose.** Beside `AssembledPackageBodySchema`: the two readings, the refusal code and the `null` caveat are true (ran); the four census sentences the prior record named are gone at head (cut `d780d37e7c`: 3 files, +7/−9, the only added tokens two punctuation marks — ran a word-multiset check).
